reason: The text demonstrates that non-leaders possess agency. The Israelites collectively act and make decisions independent of leadership direction: they cry out to God (וַיִּצְעֲקוּ בְנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶל־ יְהוָֽה), speak to Moses expressing their concerns and preferences (וַיֹּאמְרוּ אֶל־ מֹשֶׁה), observe their surroundings (אֶת־ עֵינֵיהֶם), experience fear (וַיִּֽירְאוּ), and exercise belief (וַיַּֽאֲמִינוּ בַּיהוָה וּבְמֹשֶׁה). These constitute genuine acts of agency—the capacity to act, decide, and respond—exercised by ordinary people, not only by the designated leaders (Pharaoh, Moses) or divine authority.
